observed: The main menu with New Game lit along the bottom row; the submenu bar has moved up onto Custom Character and the line beneath promises the whole points pool, scenario, trade, stats, traits and skills.

The Create World box: the name Fairport Harbor already filled in and lit, difficulty sitting at Cataclysm, the neighbours slider at Lonely, and along the middle the three choices f Finish, r Reset and a Randomize.
The Create World box with Finish now lit, and a small box in the middle of the screen asking whether I am SURE I am finished, marked case sensitive, with No framed as the standing answer.

Frame 4 was the loading screen -- Loading files, Dark Days Ahead, with a line about animals and zombies not being friends. By the time this key went out the sheet had opened on the scenario page with Evacuee standing selected and Missed further down the list.

The points page, with three ways of paying: Survivor marked current and lit, then Legacy Multiple pools and Legacy Single pool under it, and the panel on the right saying no point limits are enforced.

The points page again, the bar now down on Legacy Multiple pools, and the panel explaining that stats, traits and skills have separate pools and that stat points may be spent down into traits and skills.
The points page with Legacy Multiple pools now marked current and active, and the note that scenarios and professions come out of the skill pool.
The scenario page, Evacuee standing selected at the top with its story about reaching an evac shelter, and the points line now showing what a start costs.
The scenario page with an empty search box opened in the middle of the panel, and the budget along the top reading six for the body, none for what is wrong with me, and two for what I can do.
The search box with a single m standing in it.
The search box now reading m i.
The search box reading m i s, with the list behind it still showing every start.
The list narrowed to two, Missed and Challenge Compromised Shelter, with the panel describing a start in town across twenty-five locations and no starting neighbour, and the start costing nothing.
The top line now reads Scenario Missed, so it took, and the cursor has slid down onto Challenge Compromised Shelter behind it. The budget is unchanged at six, none and two.
The profession page, a long column of trades with Backpacker, Death Row Convict, Lawyer and Guru near the top.
The trades page with the search box open and empty.
The search box with an f in it.
The search box reading f i.
The search box reading f i s, the trades still listed behind it.
The search box reading f i s h, with the unfiltered column of trades still behind it.

The panel shows Fisher, costing two, with survival at five and athletics at two, and the kit laid out -- rod, waders, boonie hat, flannel jacket, utility vest, wrist watch, backpack, a hunting knife in a sheath, a fish trap and bait.
The top line now reads Profession Fisher beside Scenario Missed, and the budget has moved to six, none and none -- the trade cost the two I had for skills.

The background page: a long column of dependencies and licences -- heroin, sleeping pills, crack, sedatives, amphetamines, painkillers, alcohol, nicotine, caffeine -- and further down boating and driving licences, butchering, home cooking.
The background page with the search box open and empty over the list.
The search box with an n in it.
The search box reading n i.
The search box reading n i c.

The list narrowed to Nicotine Dependence, lit, and Electronic Tinkering. The panel says it earns one point, carries nicotine withdrawal at ten, and warns I will need a steady supply. Six backgrounds are already down as selected -- driving licence, home cooking, computer literate, social skills, high school graduate, mundane survival.
Nicotine Dependence has appeared at the bottom of the selected list, under the six that were already there.
The search box open and empty over the background list.
The search box with a c in it.
The search box reading c a.
The search box now legibly reading c a f over the list.
The list is down to the two caffeine entries and the lit one is the fierce version -- withdrawal at fifty, and it brings stimulant psychosis and sleepiness with it. That is not me.
The lit entry is now the plain caffeine habit -- withdrawal at ten and no traits attached to it.
Caffeine Dependence has joined the selected list and the budget has gone back to six, none and two -- the two habits paid back what the trade cost.
The search box still holding c a f from the last time I used it.

Frame 38 is unchanged from 37 and I can see why: the search box reopened already holding caf from the last time I used it, and the three letters are selected rather than empty, so rubbing out did nothing to them. The box sits over the background page, the selected list now carries eight entries with nicotine and caffeine at the bottom, and the panel offers to REMOVE caffeine dependence for a point, which I do not want. I will type over the selection instead.
The box now holds a single h where caf was.
The box reading h i.
The box reading h i g over the background list.
The list is down to High School Graduate alone and the panel says removing it refunds nothing, which is fine -- I am not doing it for points.
The schooling is off the list -- seven left, and none of them claims I finished school.
The search box open again, holding h i g from last time with the letters selected.
The box holding a single b.
The box reading b o.
The box reading b o a over the list.
The list found Boating License and the panel shows what it carries -- vehicles at intermediate, athletics at beginner, and boat piloting as a proficiency.
Boating License has gone to the top of the selected list -- eight of them now, and not one of them a lie.
The stats page: strength, dexterity, intelligence and perception all standing at eight, average human, with the cursor on strength and six left to spend on the body.
Strength has gone to nine and the five points left sit beside it.
Strength reads ten now, well above average, with four left.
The panel has moved onto dexterity, listing vehicle control, weapon damage and falling. Strength still reads ten.
The panel is on intelligence now -- bypassing vehicle locks, results from taking things apart, being paralysed by fear.
Intelligence reads seven now, below average, and the budget has come to five for the body with two still on the skills.
The panel has moved to perception -- instruments, mending clothes, critical hits.
Perception has gone to nine.
Strength ten, dexterity eight, intelligence seven, perception ten. That is me as honestly as I can put it.
The traits page, opening on a run of appearance entries -- moustaches and beards, of all things.
The search box open over the traits list.
The box holding a b.
The box holding b a.
The box holding b a c.
The box reading b a c k.
The search found Bad Back and Strong Back. The lit one earns three and says plainly that I cannot carry what a woman my strength should -- a third off, near enough. That is the one.
Bad Back is taken -- the panel now offers to give it back, which I will not be doing.
The search box open again, holding back from a moment ago with the letters selected.
The box holding a single s.
The box holding s l.
The box holding s l e.
The box holding s l e e.
The box reading s l e e p.
The search found four sleeping entries and the lit one earns a point: quite the heavy sleeper, noises unlikely to wake you.
Heavy sleeping is taken -- the panel offers it back for a point and I am leaving it where it is.
The search box open, holding sleep with the letters selected.
The box holding a single a.
The box holding a d.
The box holding a d d.
The box holding a d d i.
The box holding a d d i c.
The box now reading addict, plainly.
The search found two: Addiction Resistant sitting lit, which costs a point and says it is harder for you to become addicted -- and under it Addictive Personality.
The lit entry is Addictive Personality, earning two, saying plainly that it is easier for me to get hooked and harder to get clean.
Addictive Personality is taken -- the panel offers it back for two and I am not selling it.
The box open again with addict in it, selected.
The box holding a single t.
The box holding t o.
The box reading t o u.
The box reading t o u g.
The box reading t o u g h.
The search found Tough, lit, costing two, saying it takes a lot to bring you down -- and Tough Feet under it. The pool for what I am reads six.
Tough is taken -- the panel offers two back for it now.
The box open holding tough, selected.
The box holding a single s.
The box holding s t.
The box holding s t o.
The box reading s t o m.
The search found three: Strong Stomach at the top, then Tiny, then Weak -- and it is Weak that is standing lit, earning a point for being sick easily. That is not me.
The lit one has moved to Tiny Stomach, which is somebody's surgery, not mine.
The lit entry is Strong Stomach now, costing one, saying I am less likely to throw up and will not be left queasy if I do.
Strong Stomach is taken -- the panel offers a point back for it.
The box open holding stom, selected.
The box holding a single p.
The box holding p a.
The box holding p a c.
The box holding p a c k.
The search found Packmule alone, costing one, saying I pack efficiently and can get at things in a bag faster.
Packmule is taken. Six things down about myself -- three that are wrong with me and three that are right -- and not one of them invented.
The skills page. Every fighting skill sits at nothing for me. Survival carries five from the trade and vehicles two from the licence, and the panel offers two levels of club-swinging for a point.
The bar has moved to cutting weapons, still nothing of mine in it.
The panel offers dodging, two levels for a point.
Dodging shows two of my own, and the budget has come down by one.
The bar is on melee, nothing of mine in it.
The bar is on piercing weapons.
Unarmed combat, at nothing.
The bar has reached archery.
The bar is on handguns.
The bar is on launchers.
The bar is on marksmanship.
The bar is on rifles.
The bar is on shotguns.
The bar is on submachine guns.
The bar is on throwing.
The bar has left the weapons behind and reached applied science.
The bar is on electronics.
The bar has landed on fabrication, not electronics -- the panel offers two levels of it for a point.
Fabrication now shows two and one, and there is a list of recipes opened up beside it.
The panel offers food handling, two levels for a point.
Food handling has taken and the panel has filled with everything it opens up -- soups, sausage, sashimi, cake.
The bar is on survival and the panel offers two more levels for a point -- fish bait, cordage, traps, sleeping bags.
The panel offers tailoring, two levels for a point -- strings, pouches, ropes, cordage.
Tailoring has taken -- the panel is full of what it opens, jumpsuits and gambesons and a wetsuit.
The panel offers athletics, two levels for a point, on top of the two the trade and the licence gave me.
Athletics has taken -- two of mine on top of the two that came with the trade and the licence.
The bar is on computers, one from the schooling I kept.
The bar is on devices, at nothing.
The panel offers health care, two levels for a point, on top of the one from the everyday things.
Health care reads two and one now.
The panel offers mechanics, two levels for a point, on top of the one from the driving licence.
Mechanics reads two and one, and the ledger along the top comes out at exactly nothing left -- three on the body, two spare from what is wrong with me, five spent on what I can do.
Gender now reads Female, in pink, and the outfit beside it still says Male.
Both lines read Female now -- gender and outfit.
A box has opened asking for my age in years, minimum sixteen, with twenty-five already sitting in it.
The age box now holds a single five where the twenty-five was.
The age box reads fifty-two.
The age box has closed and the sheet is back, with the recipe lists still filling the right-hand side.
A box has opened asking for a name, and saying that cancelling will wipe it.
The name box holds a capital O.
The name box holds O d.
The name box holds O d e.
The name box holds O d e t.
The name box holds O d e t t.
The name box reads Odette.

Frame 154 is identical to 153 pixel for pixel across the name box, and the box still reads Odette. That is what a trailing space looks like: the letters do not move and the space itself draws nothing, so the screen legitimately did not change. The box is still open and waiting, so the next letter goes on the end.
The box reads Odette V.
The box reads Odette Va.
The box reads Odette Vac.
The box reads Odette Vach.
The box reads Odette Vacho.
The name box reads Odette Vachon in full.
The top line reads Odette Vachon, Missed, Fisher. That is the whole of what I came here to write down.

The summary, all of it in one place: Odette Vachon, Missed, Fisher, female. Eleven things I can do and six things I am, three of them wrong with me. Boat piloting and butchering among the proficiencies. Starting place random out of two hundred and forty-three, no vehicle. Nothing left unspent.
A box in the middle asking whether I am SURE I am finished, marked case sensitive, with Yes and No under it.

Frame 163 was the sheet with the case-sensitive box over it. The Y landed -- the blank capture that followed it was the screen going dark while the ground was being made, and the guard refused to keep it. I have since read the live screen: I am standing indoors in a golf course service building, Thursday May 20 at 08:00:00, safe mode on, wielding the fishing rod, and the message log says I missed the evacuation.

The list reads eight items, no monsters at all, and forty-four bits of furniture. Golf caps, a golf bag, gloves, tees, balls, a till with fifteen dollars in it -- and glass shards, which means a window went in somewhere.
The list is gone and I can see the room: a shop counter, chairs, lockers, a purple floor under me, and the sidebar reads Thursday May 20, 08:00:00, safe mode on, clear and bright, wielding the rod.

The chart, with a town called West Rutland spread out north of me and my own mark at the bottom of it -- a golf course service building, woods to the south and west, no water anywhere on the whole sheet.
Back in the room, clock still at eight in the morning on Thursday the twentieth, nothing moving.
A box: I have an alarm clock, and it asks whether I want to wait a while or set an alarm for later, with waiting lit.

The wait list: twenty seconds, a minute, five minutes, half an hour, one hour, two, three, six -- and further down, wait till daylight nineteen hours off, till noon four hours, till night eleven hours and fifty-four minutes.
